thread:
Maya: Incoming ticket from Acme: their prod model (redwood-model-7b-v2) p99 latency jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.9s after quant-profile rollout to mixed int8+fp8.
Acme-Infrastructure: confirmed - spike started at 2026-03-16T22:40Z right after config apply.
Maya: repro curl they sent:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\ 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\ 
 -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-model-7b-v2\",\"input\":\"summarize: long document...\",\"quant_profile\":\"int8_fp8_mixed\"}'
```
Maya: p95 also moved from ~120ms -> ~480ms, so this is a broad tail increase not just single outliers.
Jin: tagging eng-ml. @jin here. Any known regressions in mixed int8/fp8 paths or calibration flows?
Jin: I saw a perf regression in a canary last week where auto-calibration allocations grew when KV caching was enabled. Calibration maps per-shard weren't being evicted -> memory pressure -> runtime stalls.
Liam: eng-runtime — what's their typical sequence length distribution and KV cache hit rate?
Acme-Infrastructure: typical seq ~512, occasional bursts to 1024. KV cache hit ~70% during steady state.
Jin: that fits. If auto-calibrate creates per-shard calibration buffers and KV cache keeps allocations resident, GC/alloc churn can push p99 up.
Maya: they enabled the new flag `auto-calibrate: true` as part of the profile rollout.
Liam: quick mitigation we can do now: revert model to fp16 and disable auto-calibrate, then run offline calibration. Commands I used for the rollback:
```
# rollback quant to fp16
redwoodctl models set-config redwood-model-7b-v2 --quant=fp16
# disable auto-calibration
redwoodctl models set-config redwood-model-7b-v2 --auto-calibrate=false
```
Maya: applied rollback for the customer at ~2351112400 and they reported p99 dropping back to ~480ms within ~5 minutes.
Acme-Infrastructure: confirmed latency drop in our dashboards. thank you.
Jin: follow-ups (engineering): 1) add eviction policy for per-shard calibration maps 2) add soft caps on per-request calibration allocations 3) block auto-calibrate when KV cache is enabled by default (or warn loudly).
Liam: creating runtime ticket ENG-RUNTIME-3759 to add eviction + metrics + integration test that simulates KV+auto-calibrate workload.
Maya: customer requested a safer rollout plan. Proposed guardrails:
- Canary: enable new quant profile on 5% traffic for 30m
- Monitor p95/p99 and median; if p99 > 2x baseline for 10m then auto-fallback to fp16
- Disable `auto-calibrate` during initial canary; require offline calibration before full rollout
- Add an ops knob to force immediate fallback per model
Carol: customer-success: note to offer Acme a 30% credit for the hour of degraded service and schedule a post-mortem call with their infra team.
SRE-bot: deploy event: reverted quant profile for redwood-model-7b-v2 by Maya at 2351112400 :white_check_mark:
Maya: summary/action items:
- rollback completed and customer stabilized
- ENG-RUNTIME-3759 opened (eviction + metrics + test)
- Recommend offline calibration + re-profiling with smaller calibration batch sizes
- Update rollout docs to explicitly disallow `auto-calibrate=true` with KV caching enabled; add canary checklist
Jin: also recommend testing pure-int8 and pure-fp8 paths independently before enabling mixed modes; mixed paths can expose allocation/compatibility issues.
Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Acme-Infrastructure: appreciate the fast response. We'll coordinate for an offline re-calibration window.
